+// SparseCraft design point.
+// hash: 57db9c2e428dc22f   hw: e7955f4f5e66a51e   sw: f6342c9ddfeb3619
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (Sec 9o's software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS (nodes.py), but they were
+// NOT emitted here, so nothing wrote them into the tree and read_design_state
+// could not read them back: every proposal silently reverted to the defaults
+// the moment the state was re-parsed. Measured 2026-09-20 -- a run launched
+// with k_chunk=64 reported `[SW] k_chunk 64 -> 16` and reused the baseline's
+// sw_hash, i.e. the whole software half of co-design was inert, for the agent
+// and the CLI alike.
+//
+// k_chunk stays 16 across the DIM 16 -> 32 move (iteration 6). The staging
+// requirement is k_chunk*DIM rows of A plus k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM rows of B:
+// at DIM = 32 that is 16*32 = 512 rows of 32 B (16 KB) plus 16*2*32 = 1024
+// rows of 32 B (32 KB) = 48 KB, comfortably inside the 256 KB scratchpad.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): off_chip_bytes measured at 3,211,264 B, of
+// which RDMA_BYTES_REC = 3,080,192 is the repeated re-fetch of the dense X
+// operand once per K-pass. At 22 pJ/byte that is ~71 of the 95.7 uJ total, so
+// DRAM, not MAC and not SRAM, is the dominant energy term. Holding all 32 X
+// slices resident in the 256 KB scratchpad removes the re-fetch entirely and
+// also removes the mvin traffic that the diagnosis blames for the
+// scratchpad-wait stalls behind exe_active = 0.39.
+// MEASURED: cycles 106,650 -> 79,433 (-25.5%), energy 95.7 -> 32.2 uJ (-66.3%),
+// off_chip_bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680. Confirmed: the DRAM term is now gone.
+// X is 2,048 rows of 16 B at DIM = 16; at DIM = 32 it is 1,024 rows of 32 B.
+// Identical 32 KB, so residency survives the geometry change unchanged.
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields, until Phase 3 adds the corresponding Chisel
+// parameters -- emitting them as `.copy(gate_enable = ...)` before the field
+// exists makes elaboration fail with a Scala type error.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 3). With DRAM removed, the array itself is the
+// remaining energy term and the bottleneck is compute (exe_active = 0.90).
+// The counters say macs_issued = 8,388,608 against macs_useful = 524,288:
+// 93.75% of every multiply the mesh performs has a zero streaming operand and
+// is currently being computed densely, because the T-A datapath exists in
+// PE.scala but SparseCraftRTL.gateEnable has been false for both measured
+// iterations. This turns it on. Energy only -- a gated PE still occupies its
+// pipeline slot, so cycles are unchanged by construction; the risk axis is
+// Fmax (a zero-comparator in front of the MAC) and therefore t.
+// MEASURED (iteration 3): MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 of 8,388,608 issued, so
+// the gate fires on 93.75% of multiplies exactly as predicted -- and energy
+// moved only 32.235 -> 30.111 uJ (-6.6%). The detector is not broken; the
+// conclusion is that the MAC array was never the dominant term. Gating 93.75%
+// of every multiply in a 16x16 INT8 mesh bought 2.1 uJ, so the whole switched
+// multiplier capacity is worth at most ~2.3 uJ of the 30.1 uJ that remains.
+// Fmax did not move (t flat), so T-A is kept: it is a pure, paid-for win.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 4). This is the one sanctioned technique that
+// has never been measured, and the iteration-3 result is what points at it.
+// Accounting for the 30.111 uJ that is left:
+//   DRAM        327,680 B at ~22 pJ/B  ~=  7.2 uJ
+//   MAC array   bounded above by the T-A delta        ~=  2.3 uJ
+//   remainder                                         ~= 20.6 uJ
+// The remainder is scratchpad SRAM traffic. x_resident = 1 (iteration 2) is
+// what created it: it deliberately traded DRAM re-fetch for on-chip residency,
+// so every operand element the mesh consumes now comes out of a 256 KB SRAM
+// instead of off-chip. That was a 66% energy win and it is not being undone --
+// but it relocated the dominant energy term from DRAM into the scratchpad, and
+// the scratchpad read is precisely what T-B suppresses.
+// MEASURED (iteration 4): energy 30.111 -> 24.836 uJ (-17.5%), cycles flat at
+// 79,433 exactly as predicted, area +4.2%. So the ZBU removed ~5.3 uJ of the
+// ~20.6 uJ SRAM term, leaving ~15 uJ of scratchpad reads standing. Kept.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 1
+//
+// ==================== ITERATION 6: meshRows/Columns 16 -> 32 ==============
+//
+// Three consecutive measured iterations have left cycles pinned at exactly
+// 79,433, and that is structural, not accidental: BOTH sanctioned sparsity
+// mechanisms are cycle-flat by wiring in this build. T-A gates a multiplier
+// that still occupies its pipeline slot; T-B's sc_skip gates only
+// `mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)`, while `ren`, `q.io.enq.valid` and
+// `io.read.req.ready` remain stock, so a skipped row still consumes its slot
+// and still returns a response. The execute-side preload/compute suppression
+// that would buy 2*DIM cycles lives in ExecuteController.scala, which is not
+// writable. No amount of further sparsity work can move `time` here.
+//
+// What CAN move it is the geometry, and the counters say so directly. The
+// diagnosis is `compute` with exe_active = 0.8953, and the work is dense-
+// equivalent: macs_issued = 8,388,608 = 512 * 64 * 256 = M*N*K, a figure that
+// does not depend on DIM. A DIM x DIM mesh retires DIM^2 of them per issued
+// cycle, so the mesh-occupancy floor is
+//
+//     DIM = 16 -> 8,388,608 / 256  = 32,768 issue-cycles
+//     DIM = 32 -> 8,388,608 / 1024 =  8,192 issue-cycles
+//
+// a 4x reduction in the only term the diagnosis names as binding. The
+// measured 79,433 sits 2.4x above the DIM = 16 floor (preload turnaround plus
+// spad_read_delay = 4 refill), and that overhead is per-tile, so it shrinks
+// with the tile count as well.
+//
+// The same move is an SRAM-energy move, which is where the remaining ~15 uJ
+// lives. Operand reads for an M*N*K product on a DIM x DIM mesh are
+// M*K*(N/DIM) for A plus K*N*(M/DIM) for B -- both inversely proportional to
+// DIM. Doubling DIM halves total scratchpad read traffic outright, on top of
+// whatever the ZBU suppresses. This is the lever that attacks the dominant
+// energy term, not just the residual MAC term.
+//
+// WHAT I AM SPENDING: area. PE count 256 -> 1024, so the array quadruples and
+// total area should rise on the order of +30-40%. That is a deliberate,
+// stated trade of the area axis for the time and energy axes; Pareto
+// admission is non-dominance, not improvement on all three.
+//
+// Legality re-checked at DIM = 32, since every geometry constraint is a
+// function of it:
+//   square power of 2: 32*1 == 32*1, >= 2                            OK
+//   spad rows/bank:    256 KB / 4 banks / 32 B per row = 2,048       OK
+//                      (power of 2, multiple of DIM = 32)
+//   acc rows/bank:     64 KB / 2 banks / 128 B per row = 256         OK
+//   sp_banks = 4 >= 3                                                OK
+//   Little's Law:      64 * 64 = 4,096, unchanged by geometry        OK
+//   granule | DIM:     32 | 32                                       OK
+//   mvin_scale_shared: still false (8 != 32)                         OK
+//
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 32
+//
+// granule_size tracks DIM and that is forced, not chosen. The ZBU's read
+// suppression is a SyncReadMem read enable, which is ONE bit for the WHOLE
+// row; there is no sub-row enable to drive, so a granule finer than the row
+// could only be consumed by AND-ing its sub-flags back up to a row flag --
+// bitwise identical skips at 2x/4x the bitmap area. The row is DIM elements
+// wide, so DIM = 32 makes the granule 32. The cost is real and I am naming it
+// in advance: at 93.75% element-level zero density the all-zero-row rate
+// falls from 0.9375^16 = 36% to 0.9375^32 = 13%, so the ZBU's HIT RATE drops.
+// It is still the right trade, because the population it is hitting halves at
+// the same time -- total A-read energy goes as (reads) * (1 - hit rate), i.e.
+// 0.5 * 0.87 = 0.43 of the DIM = 16 figure, against 1.0 * 0.64 = 0.64 today.
+// If iteration 7 shows the ZBU contribution collapsing, the follow-up is to
+// re-measure T-B's delta at DIM = 32 before spending more bitmap on it.
+//
+// zbu_operand stays A: A is the 93.75%-zero streaming operand. X is dense and
+// resident, so a bitmap over it would never fire.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // 16 -> 32: the mesh-occupancy floor is macs_issued / DIM^2, and the
+    // measured diagnosis is compute-bound at exe_active = 0.90 with both
+    // sparsity mechanisms cycle-flat by wiring. See the note above.
+    meshRows    = 32,
+    meshColumns = 32,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // Capacities deliberately UNCHANGED so the geometry delta is attributable.
+    // The row width doubles with DIM, so rows/bank halve to 2,048 (spad) and
+    // 256 (acc) -- both still powers of 2 and multiples of DIM = 32.
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(256),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+
+    // --- L5 address generation / DMA ---
+    // dma_buswidth stays 128. off_chip_bytes = 327,680 over 79,433 cycles is

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit. Conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ==================== DESIGN NOTES (iteration 4) ====================
+  *
+  * GRANULE = w bits = DIM elements = one row, and that is not a free choice
+  * here, it is forced by the wiring. Scratchpad.scala suppresses the read with
+  *
+  *     mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)
+  *
+  * `mem` is a SyncReadMem whose read enable is ONE bit for the WHOLE row.
+  * There is no sub-row read enable to drive, so a granule finer than the row
+  * could only be consumed by AND-ing all the sub-granule flags of a row back
+  * together -- which is bitwise identical to the row flag, at 2x/4x/16x the
+  * bitmap area and a deeper reduce. Finer granularity in THIS build is
+  * strictly dominated: more area, more delay, exactly the same skips. Hence
+  * granule_size stays at 16 (= DIM = one row) and the lever I actually move
+  * is detector pipeline depth, below.
+  *
+  * DETECTOR PIPELINE DEPTH (the real change vs. the seed).
+  * The seed did the whole detector in the write cycle:
+  *
+  *     when (write_fire) { bitmap(write_addr) := write_full && (write_data === 0.U) }
+  *
+  * which puts a w-wide (128b) OR-reduce IN SERIES with a 4096-entry one-hot
+  * write decoder inside a single cycle, and the bitmap is a flat register file
+  * whose 4096:1 read mux already sits in series with the SRAM read enable.
+  * Both halves of the ZBU landed on the same clock period, and Fmax is the
+  * axis T-B is most likely to lose on -- t is cycles x MEASURED period, so an
+  * energy win paid for in period is not a win.
+  *
+  * So the detector is split into two stages: cycle 0 reduces the data and
+  * latches (addr, bit); cycle 1 commits it into the bitmap. The OR-reduce and
+  * the write decoder are now in different cycles.
+  *
+  * WHY THE PIPELINE IS STILL BIT-EXACT.
+  * A one-cycle-late bitmap update creates exactly one hazard: a read issued in
+  * the shadow cycle sees the PRE-write bit. If the pending write is making a
+  * previously-zero row NONZERO, that stale bit is SET and we would skip a read
+  * of real data -- silent corruption, the exact failure mode the header warns
+  * about. `hazard` kills the skip for any read whose address matches the
+  * in-flight write, so the shadow cycle degrades to "read it densely", which
+  * is always safe. The converse case (pending write makes the row zero, we
+  * fail to skip) costs one missed skip and cannot corrupt.
+  * The comparator sits in PARALLEL with the bitmap mux, not in series, so it
+  * adds one 2-input AND to the read path, not a second mux tree.
+  *
+  * The bit is set only on a FULL-WIDTH all-zero write. A masked write clears
+  * it unconditionally -- the row is then partly unknown, and "unknown" must
+  * read as "not provably zero".
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule.
+  // RESET VALUE IS false = "not provably zero" = conservative. A bitmap that
+  // comes out of reset all-ones would skip reads of rows that were never
+  // written, which is the corruption case.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // ---- stage 0: detect. w-wide OR-reduce, ends at a flop. ----
+  // `!orR` rather than `=== 0.U` so the reduce is emitted as a balanced tree
+  // instead of a w-bit equality against a constant.
+  val row_is_zero = !io.write_data.orR
+  val new_bit     = io.write_full && row_is_zero
+
+  val pend_valid = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val pend_addr  = RegEnable(io.write_addr, io.write_fire)
+  val pend_bit   = RegEnable(new_bit,       io.write_fire)
+
+  // ---- stage 1: commit. One-hot decode over n entries, starts at a flop. ----
+  when (pend_valid) {
+    bitmap(pend_addr) := pend_bit
+  }
+
+  // ---- read: bitmap lookup, with the shadow-cycle write hazard suppressed. ----
+  val hazard = pend_valid && (pend_addr === io.read_addr)
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en && !hazard
+}
